summary: This segment details the pathways of precipitation after reaching land, focusing on infiltration processes influenced by soil and environmental factors, subsurface water movement (percolation), and the mechanics of groundwater storage within aquifers that sustain surface water flow.
topics: Infiltration factors (soil structure, moisture, vegetation, rainfall intensity)
Subsurface water movement (absorption, pore retention, percolation)

summary: Surface runoff is generated by gravity-driven flow over land when precipitation exceeds infiltration capacity or soil saturation, moving toward channels and rivers within a watershed defined as the draining area. Water storage and movement operate across varying timescales involving temporary retention in lakes, wetlands, snow, and ice, rather than a single compulsory loop.
